questions.question:
Find the average of the following sets of numbers.

693, 456, 876, 532, 934, 691, 596, 398, 682
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Assume a base average of 600 and calculate deviations from it.

Deviations: +93, −144, +276, −68, +334, +91, −4, −202, +82

Sum of deviations = (93 + 276 + 334 + 91 + 82) − (144 + 68 + 4 + 202) = 876 − 418 = 458

Average deviation = 458 ÷ 9 ≈ 50.89

Actual Average = 600 + 50.89 = 650.89

**∴ The correct answer is 650.89.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given observations: 693, 456, 876, 532, 934, 691, 596, 398, 682

Formula used: Average = Sum of observations ÷ Total number of observations

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/41745a5b1aabf51935adfcd6f9f6149e0c87d71edc40330f088cccb3886910bb.png] 

⇒ Sum = 693 + 456 + 876 + 532 + 934 + 691 + 596 + 398 + 682

⇒ Sum = 5858

⇒ Total count of numbers (n) = 9

⇒ Average = 5858 ÷ 9

⇒ Average = 650.8888...

**∴ The correct answer is 650.89.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Sum of Deviations

The sum of the deviations of a set of observations from their arithmetic mean is always zero. ∑(xᵢ − x̄) = 0.

Scaling Property

If every observation in a data set is increased/decreased by a constant 'k', the new average also increases/decreases by 'k'.

Combined Average Formula

If two groups have sizes n₁, n₂ and averages a₁, a₂, the combined average is (n₁a₁ + n₂a₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).</p

questions.question: The largest three-digit number that gives the same remainder 2 when divided by 3, 5 and 9 is ________.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Check the divisibility rule for 5: A number leaving remainder 2 when divided by 5 must end in 2 or 7.

Looking at the options: (1) 999, (2) 984, (3) 998, (4) 992.

Only 992 ends in 2, satisfying the condition for 5.

Verify for 9: Sum of digits of 992 = 9 + 9 + 2 = 20. 20 ÷ 9 leaves remainder 2.

**∴ The correct answer is 992.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Divisors = 3, 5, 9; Common Remainder = 2.

**Formula:** Number = LCM(divisors) × k + Remainder

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6b3ba400e3375feb23115995477ef30d35ea0f5cf874f640e8377eb5a68f3aeb.png] 

⇒ LCM of 3, 5, and 9:

⇒ 3 = 3¹

⇒ 5 = 5¹

⇒ 9 = 3²

⇒ LCM = 3² × 5 = 9 × 5 = 45

⇒ The largest three-digit number is 999.

⇒ Divide 999 by 45: 999 ÷ 45 = 22 with remainder 9.

⇒ Largest multiple of 45 below 1000 = 999 − 9 = 990.

⇒ Required number = 990 + 2 = 992.

**∴ The correct answer is 992.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

LCM and Remainder Case 1

When a number is divided by x, y, and z leaving the same remainder R in each case, the number is of the form [LCM(x, y, z) × k] + R.

LCM and Remainder Case 2

When a number leaves different remainders a, b, c such that (x−a) = (y−b) = (z−c) = K, the number is of the form [LCM(x, y, z) × k] − K.

Divisibility Rule of 9

A number is divisible by 9 if the sum of its digits is divisible by 9. The remainder left when the sum is divided by 9 is the same as the remainder of the original number.</p

questions.question: A person can hit a target 5 times out of 8 shots. If he fires 10 shots, what is the probability that he will hit the target twice?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Identify parameters: n = 10 shots, r = 2 hits, p (hit) = 5/8, q (miss) = 3/8.

Apply Binomial Probability formula: P(X = r) = ⁿCᵣ × pr × qⁿ−r.

Calculation: ¹⁰C₂ × (5/8)² × (3/8)⁸ = 45 × (25/8²) × (3⁸/8⁸).

Simplified result: (45 × 25 × 3⁸) / 8¹⁰ = (1125 × 3⁸) / 8¹⁰.

**∴ The correct answer is (1125 × 3⁸) / 8¹⁰.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total shots (n) = 10

Shots to hit (r) = 2

Probability of hitting (p) = 5/8

Probability of missing (q) = 1 − 5/8 = 3/8

**Formula Used:**

P(X = k) = ⁿCₖ × pk × qⁿ−k

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/301b7669421a16770b33a7993fa3c5ded23e8ee626c63daecd1985b0c1224607.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ ¹⁰C₂ = (10 × 9) / (2 × 1) = 45

⇒ P(X = 2) = 45 × (5/8)² × (3/8)¹⁰−²

⇒ P(X = 2) = 45 × (5² / 8²) × (3⁸ / 8⁸)

⇒ P(X = 2) = 45 × (25 / 8²) × (3⁸ / 8⁸)

⇒ P(X = 2) = (45 × 25 × 3⁸) / 8⁽²⁺⁸⁾

⇒ P(X = 2) = (1125 × 3⁸) / 8¹⁰

**∴ The correct answer is (1125 × 3⁸) / 8¹⁰.**

**__Additional Information__**

Binomial Distribution Conditions

It applies when there are a fixed number of independent trials (n), each with only two possible outcomes (success/failure) and a constant probability of success (p).

Binomial Mean and Variance

The mean of a Binomial distribution is given by μ = np, and the variance is given by σ² = npq, where q = 1 − p.

Combination Formula

The number of ways to choose r successes out of n trials is ⁿCᵣ = n! / [r! × (n−r)!].</p

questions.question: The angle of elevation of the top of a tower from the top of a building whose height is 680 m is 45° and the angle of elevation of the top of same tower from the foot of the same building is 60°. What is the height (in m) of the tower?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In height and distance, for a tower height H and building height h, if angles are θ₁ (from top) and θ₂ (from foot):

H = h × tan(θ₂) ÷ (tan(θ₂) − tan(θ₁))

Given θ₁ = 45°, θ₂ = 60°, h = 680 m

H = 680 × √3 ÷ (√3 − 1) = [680√3 × (√3 + 1)] ÷ [(√3 − 1)(√3 + 1)]

H = 680(3 + √3) ÷ 2 = 340(3 + √3)

**∴ The correct answer is 340(3 + √3) m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Height of building (CD) = 680 m

Angle of elevation from top of building (C) to top of tower (A) = 45°

Angle of elevation from foot of building (D) to top of tower (A) = 60°

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2cf154696b6333362306d29f15c7cb2b5c764427e46cf46763b926d1621b5423.png] 

**Formula Used:**

tan(θ) = Perpendicular ÷ Base

**Calculations:**

Let the height of the tower be H and the distance between the building and the tower be x.

In right-angled triangle above the building height:

⇒ tan(45°) = (H − 680) ÷ x

⇒ 1 = (H − 680) ÷ x

⇒ x = H − 680 --- (1)

In right-angled triangle from the foot of the building:

⇒ tan(60°) = H ÷ x

⇒ √3 = H ÷ x

⇒ x = H ÷ √3 --- (2)

Equating (1) and (2):

⇒ H − 680 = H ÷ √3

⇒ H√3 − 680√3 = H

⇒ H(√3 − 1) = 680√3

⇒ H = (680√3) ÷ (√3 − 1)

Rationalizing the denominator:

⇒ H = [680√3 × (√3 + 1)] ÷ [(√3 − 1)(√3 + 1)]

⇒ H = [680(3 + √3)] ÷ (3 − 1)

⇒ H = [680(3 + √3)] ÷ 2

⇒ H = 340(3 + √3)

**∴ The correct answer is 340(3 + √3) m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Angle of Elevation

The angle formed by the line of sight with the horizontal when looking up at an object.

Standard Trigonometric Ratios

tan 30° = 1/√3, tan 45° = 1, tan 60° = √3.

Height and Distance Shortcut

If distances x₁ and x₂ are measured from the foot for angles α and β, then height H = (x₂ − x₁) / (cot α − cot β).</p

questions.question: The median of a set of 11 distinct observations is 73.2. If each of the largest five observations of the set is increased by 3, then the median of the new set:

options.text: is 3 times that of the original set
remains the same as that of the original set

The largest five observations are the 7th, 8th, 9th, 10th, and 11th terms.

Increasing values that are already larger than the median does not change the position or value of the median (the 6th term).

Since the 6th term remains 73.2, the median of the new set remains unchanged.

**∴ The correct answer is remains the same as that of the original set.**

**Given:**

Total observations (n) = 11

⇒ New observations = x₁, x₂, x₃, x₄, x₅, x₆, (x₇+3), (x₈+3), (x₉+3), (x₁₀+3), (x₁₁+3).

⇒ Since x₆ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Median for Odd vs Even n

If n is odd, Median = ((n+1)/2)th term. If n is even, Median = Average of (n/2)th and ((n/2)+1)th terms.

Property of Median

The median is not affected by extreme values or changes in values that do not cross the central position in the ordered list.

Effect of Linear Changes

If every observation in a set is increased by a constant k, the median also increases by k. However, if only specific observations are changed, the median may or may not change depending on their position.</p

questions.question: In a trapezium ABCD, AD and BC are parallel to each other with a perpendicular distance of 8 m between them. Also, (AB) = (CD) = 10 m, and (AD) = 15 m, (AD) < (BC). What is the perimeter (in m) of the trapezium ABCD?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For an isosceles trapezium where AB = CD and AD || BC:

Bottom Base (BC) = AD + 2 × √(Slant Side² − Height²)

BC = 15 + 2 × √(10² − 8²) = 15 + 2 × 6 = 27 m

Perimeter = Sum of all sides = AD + BC + AB + CD

Perimeter = 15 + 27 + 10 + 10 = 62 m

**∴ The correct answer is 62 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** AD = 15 m, AB = 10 m, CD = 10 m, and Height (h) = 8 m.

**Formula:** Perimeter = AD + BC + AB + CD

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9ed9cc19d3a42c7844075d2bde9183566bda603d49953c47d7f24dc94f2def66.png] 

In the trapezium ABCD, let's drop perpendiculars AM and DN on base BC.

⇒ AM = DN = 8 m (Height)

⇒ In right-angled triangle AMB, by Pythagoras theorem:

⇒ BM² = AB² − AM²

⇒ BM² = 10² − 8² = 100 − 64 = 36

⇒ BM = 6 m

⇒ Since the trapezium is isosceles (AB = CD), BM = NC = 6 m.

⇒ Length of base BC = BM + MN + NC

⇒ As MN = AD, BC = 6 + 15 + 6 = 27 m

⇒ Perimeter of ABCD = AB + BC + CD + DA

⇒ Perimeter = 10 + 27 + 10 + 15

⇒ Perimeter = 62 m

**∴ The correct answer is 62 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Area of a Trapezium

The area of a trapezium is calculated as Area = 1/2 × (sum of parallel sides) × height = 1/2 × (a + b) × h.

Isosceles Trapezium Properties

In an isosceles trapezium, the non-parallel sides are equal, the base angles are equal, and the diagonals are equal in length.

Median of a Trapezium

The median (or midsegment) of a trapezium is parallel to the bases and its length is the average of the base lengths: Median = (a + b) / 2.</p

questions.question: A prism and a pyramid have the same base and the same height. Find the ratio of the volumes of the prism and the pyramid.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**3 : 1**__
**__Key Points__**
__

• The **Volume of a Prism** is calculated by multiplying the **Base Area** (A) by the **Vertical Height** (h). The formula is given as: **Vₚᵣᵢₛₘ = Base Area × Height**.

• The **Volume of a Pyramid** is exactly one-third of the volume of a prism that has the same **Base Area** and **Height**. The formula is given as: **Vₚyᵣₐₘᵢd = (1/3) × Base Area × Height**.

• In this problem, it is stated that both the **Prism** and the **Pyramid** share the same **Base Area** (let it be **'A'**) and the same **Height** (let it be **'h'**).

• To find the **Ratio** of their volumes, we set up the expression: **Volume of Prism : Volume of Pyramid**.

• Substituting the formulas: **(A × h) : ((1/3) × A × h)**.

• By simplifying the expression and dividing both sides by **(A × h)**, we get **1 : 1/3**.

• Multiplying both sides by **3** to clear the fraction, the ratio becomes **3 : 1**.

• Therefore, the volume of a prism is **three times** the volume of a pyramid with the same base and height.

**Additional Information__**

• A **Prism** is a three-dimensional solid with two **congruent** and **parallel** bases. The lateral faces are typically **parallelograms** (or rectangles in a right prism).

• A **Pyramid** is a three-dimensional solid with a **polygonal base** and triangular lateral faces that meet at a single point called the **Apex**.

• The relationship **Vₚᵣᵢₛₘ = 3 × Vₚyᵣₐₘᵢd** holds true regardless of the shape of the base (triangle, square, hexagon, etc.), as long as the base and height are identical for both solids.

• Similarly, the volume of a **Cylinder** is three times the volume of a **Cone** if they have the same **radius** and **height**.

questions.question: If two LED TVs and one mobile phone cost ₹31,000, while two mobile phones and one LED TV cost ₹35,000, then the value of one mobile phone is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Total cost of 3 LED TVs and 3 Mobiles = 31,000 + 35,000 = 66,000

⇒ 1 LED TV + 1 Mobile = 66,000 ÷ 3 = 22,000

Given: 1 LED TV + 2 Mobiles = 35,000

⇒ 1 Mobile = (1 LED TV + 2 Mobiles) − (1 LED TV + 1 Mobile) = 35,000 − 22,000 = 13,000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹13,000.**

**__Alternate Method__**

Given values:

Cost of 2 LED TVs + 1 Mobile = ₹31,000

Cost of 1 LED TV + 2 Mobiles = ₹35,000

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f5304d38705cb50f0305f2ec034dc34d1de5896a07ef4c68d4eba0d2eb6c960d.png] 

Let the cost of one LED TV be T and the cost of one Mobile be M.

Equation 1: 2T + M = 31,000

Equation 2: T + 2M = 35,000

⇒ Multiply Equation 2 by 2:

⇒ 2(T + 2M) = 2 × 35,000

⇒ 2T + 4M = 70,000 --- (Equation 3)

⇒ Subtract Equation 1 from Equation 3:

⇒ (2T + 4M) − (2T + M) = 70,000 − 31,000

⇒ 3M = 39,000

⇒ M = 39,000 ÷ 3

⇒ M = 13,000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹13,000.**

**__Additional Information__**

Elimination Method

Variables are eliminated by making the coefficients of one variable equal in both equations through multiplication.

Substitution Method

Express one variable in terms of the other from one equation and substitute it into the second equation.

System of Linear Equations

A set of two or more equations with the same variables. For two variables x and y, the general form is a₁x + b₁y = c₁ and a₂x + b₂y = c₂.

questions.question: What is the volume of a cylinder if the radius of the cylinder is 10 cm and height is 20 cm? (Take π = 3.14)
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Volume of a cylinder is given by the formula πr²h.

Given: r = 10 cm, h = 20 cm, π = 3.14

Direct Calculation: 3.14 × 10 × 10 × 20

⇒ 314 × 20 = 6280 cm³

**∴ The correct answer is 6280 cm³.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Radius of cylinder (r) = 10 cm

Height of cylinder (h) = 20 cm

Value of π = 3.14

**Formula Used:**

Volume of a cylinder = πr²h

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/39d0c8a415a08eecea11fc0143cc9fee95f150e6bbc1e2b701c90ee813e758c6.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Volume = 3.14 × (10)² × 20

⇒ Volume = 3.14 × 100 × 20

⇒ Volume = 314 × 20

⇒ Volume = 6280 cm³

**∴ The correct answer is 6280 cm³.**

**__Additional Information__**

Curved Surface Area (CSA)

The curved surface area of a cylinder is given by the formula 2πrh.

Total Surface Area (TSA)

The total surface area of a cylinder includes both the curved area and the two circular bases: TSA = 2πr(h + r).

Volume of a Cone

A cone with the same radius and height as a cylinder has exactly one-third of its volume: V = (1/3)πr²h.</p

questions.question: P, Q, and R can finish a work in 5 days, 10 days, and 15 days, respectively, working alone. P and Q work on the first day, P and R work on the second day and P and Q work on the third day, and so on till the work is completed. In how many days the work will be completed?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Total Work = LCM(5, 10, 15) = 30 units.

Efficiencies: P = 6, Q = 3, R = 2.

Day 1 (P+Q) = 9 units; Day 2 (P+R) = 8 units.

In 2 days, work completed = 9 + 8 = 17 units.

Day 3 (P+Q) = 9 units; Total after 3 days = 17 + 9 = 26 units.

Remaining 4 units done by (P+R) on Day 4 in 4 ÷ 8 = 1/2 day.

**∴ The correct answer is 7/2 days.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by P = 5 days

Time taken by Q = 10 days

Time taken by R = 15 days

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = LCM of individual time periods

Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time

 
 

 **Person**
 **Days**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total work = 30 units

⇒ Work on Day 1 (P + Q) = 6 + 3 = 9 units

⇒ Work on Day 2 (P + R) = 6 + 2 = 8 units

⇒ Combined work in first 2 days = 9 + 8 = 17 units

⇒ Remaining work after 2 days = 30 − 17 = 13 units

⇒ Work on Day 3 (P + Q) = 9 units

⇒ Remaining work after 3 days = 13 − 9 = 4 units

⇒ Efficiency of (P + R) on Day 4 = 6 + 2 = 8 units/day

⇒ Time taken for remaining 4 units = 4 ÷ 8 = 1/2 day

⇒ Total time = 3 + 1/2 = 7/2 days

**∴ The correct answer is 7/2 days.**

**__Additional Information__**

Alternate Day Work Concept

When people work on alternate days, identify the work done in one complete cycle and then calculate the number of full cycles that fit into the total work.

Work and Wages

If a group of people work together or on alternate days, the total wages are always distributed in the ratio of the actual units of work done by each individual.

Pipes and Cisterns

Similar to time and work, but if a pipe empties the tank, its efficiency is taken as negative. Total capacity is found using LCM of the time taken by individual pipes.</p

questions.question: A goods train 350 m long passes through a tunnel of length 1250 m in 80 seconds. What is the speed of the train?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Total Distance to cover = Length of Train + Length of Tunnel = 350 + 1250 = 1600 m

Speed (in m/s) = Total Distance ÷ Time = 1600 ÷ 80 = 20 m/s

To convert m/s to km/h, multiply by 18/5:

Speed (in km/h) = 20 × (18 ÷ 5) = 4 × 18 = 72 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 72 km/h.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of the goods train (LT) = 350 m

Length of the tunnel (LP) = 1250 m

Time taken (t) = 80 seconds

**Formula Used:**

Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

Total Distance = Length of Train + Length of Tunnel

Speed (km/h) = Speed (m/s) × (18 ÷ 5)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e23474f515a5fe090ee2919142b697ac0953628fd2d95ec62cfc62f54d989455.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Distance = 350 + 1250 = 1600 m

⇒ Speed in m/s = 1600 ÷ 80

⇒ Speed in m/s = 20 m/s

⇒ Speed in km/h = 20 × (18 ÷ 5)

⇒ Speed in km/h = 4 × 18

⇒ Speed in km/h = 72 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 72 km/h.**

**__Additional Information__**

Speed Conversion Rules

To convert speed from km/h to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert from m/s to km/h, multiply by 18/5.

Train Crossing Stationary Objects

When a train crosses a stationary point object (pole, tree, man), distance = length of train. When it crosses an object with length (bridge, platform, tunnel), distance = length of train + length of object.

Relative Speed

If two objects move in the same direction, relative speed = S₁ − S₂. If they move in opposite directions, relative speed = S₁ + S₂.</p

questions.question: If one of the interior angles of a regular polygon is (15)/(16) times of one of the interior angles of a regular decagon, then find the number of diagonals of the polygon.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Interior angle of a decagon (10 sides) = (10 − 2) × 180° ÷ 10 = 144°.

Interior angle of the polygon = 15/16 × 144° = 15 × 9° = 135°.

Exterior angle = 180° − 135° = 45°.

Number of sides (n) = 360° ÷ 45° = 8.

Number of diagonals = n(n − 3) ÷ 2 = 8 × 5 ÷ 2 = 20.

The sum of all interior angles of a polygon with 'n' sides is given by (n − 2) × 180°.

Append y: The number 1y must be divisible by 7.

**∴ The correct answer is 4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Number = 463y

A number is divisible by 7 if the result of subtracting twice the last digit from the number formed by the remaining digits is divisible by 7.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/38059b04fadc10b3344291f65f92f6f908ef4249d600ae351d9164b3218da922.png]

⇒ y = 7 − 3

⇒ y = 4

Check with divisibility rule: 463 − 2(4) = 463 − 8 = 455.

Divisibility Rule of 7

Subtract twice the last digit from the rest of the number. If the result is 0 or a multiple of 7, the original number is divisible by 7.

Divisibility Rule of 11

The difference between the sum of digits at odd places and the sum of digits at even places must be either 0 or a multiple of 11.

Divisibility Rule of 13

Add four times the last digit to the remaining number. If the sum is divisible by 13, the original number is divisible by 13.</p

questions.question: If a cot θ + b cosec θ = p and b cot θ + a cosec θ = q then p² - q² is equal to _________.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Assume a specific value for θ to simplify the calculation, let θ = 90°.

Then, cot 90° = 0 and cosec 90° = 1.

Substitute these values: p = a(0) + b(1) = b and q = b(0) + a(1) = a.

Now, calculate p² − q² = b² − a².

**∴ The correct answer is b² − a².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

p = a cot θ + b cosec θ

q = b cot θ + a cosec θ

**Formula Used:**

(x + y)² = x² + y² + 2xy

cosec² θ − cot² θ = 1

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1deb6edc701424e631b58500b9b9a03604ace626509ace60b71d44c1a0659e8f.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ p² = (a cot θ + b cosec θ)²

⇒ p² = a² cot² θ + b² cosec² θ + 2ab cot θ cosec θ ----(1)

⇒ q² = (b cot θ + a cosec θ)²

⇒ q² = b² cot² θ + a² cosec² θ + 2ab cot θ cosec θ ----(2)

⇒ Subtracting (2) from (1):

⇒ p² − q² = (a² − b²) cot² θ + (b² − a²) cosec² θ

⇒ p² − q² = −(b² − a²) cot² θ + (b² − a²) cosec² θ

⇒ p² − q² = (b² − a²) (cosec² θ − cot² θ)

⇒ Since cosec² θ − cot² θ = 1,

⇒ p² − q² = (b² − a²)(1)

**∴ The correct answer is b² − a².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Trigonometric Pythagorean Identities

Standard identities used in simplification: sin² θ + cos² θ = 1, sec² θ − tan² θ = 1, and cosec² θ − cot² θ = 1.

Value Substitution Method

This method is highly effective in MCQ exams for identities. Common values used are 0°, 45°, and 90°, provided the function is defined at that point.

Reciprocal Relations

cosec θ = 1 ÷ sin θ and cot θ = cos θ ÷ sin θ.</p

questions.question: PQRS is a cyclic quadrilateral. If ∠P is three times of ∠R and ∠S is four times of ∠Q, then the sum of ∠S + ∠R will be:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of opposite angles: ∠P : ∠R = 3 : 1 ⇒ Total 4 units = 180°

Value of ∠R = 1 unit = 180° ÷ 4 = 45°

Ratio of opposite angles: ∠S : ∠Q = 4 : 1 ⇒ Total 5 units = 180°

Value of ∠S = 4 units = (180° ÷ 5) × 4 = 144°

Sum ∠S + ∠R = 144° + 45° = 189°

**∴ The correct answer is 189°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Quadrilateral PQRS is cyclic.

∠P = 3 × ∠R

∠S = 4 × ∠Q

**Formula Used:**

In a cyclic quadrilateral, the sum of opposite angles is 180°.

∠P + ∠R = 180°

∠Q + ∠S = 180°

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4abf6994ea48a35281374c1889cd34c3a17ab8a9799cadb6f9df5b939d416519.png] 

**Calculations:**

Case 1: ∠P and ∠R are opposite angles.

⇒ ∠P + ∠R = 180°

⇒ 3∠R + ∠R = 180°

⇒ 4∠R = 180°

⇒ ∠R = 45°

Case 2: ∠S and ∠Q are opposite angles.

⇒ ∠S + ∠Q = 180°

⇒ ∠S + (∠S ÷ 4) = 180°

⇒ (5 × ∠S) ÷ 4 = 180°

⇒ 5∠S = 720°

⇒ ∠S = 144°

Now, finding the required sum:

⇒ Sum = ∠S + ∠R

⇒ Sum = 144° + 45°

⇒ Sum = 189°

**∴ The correct answer is 189°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Cyclic Quadrilateral Property

A quadrilateral is called cyclic if all its four vertices lie on a circle. The sum of any pair of opposite angles is 180°.

Exterior Angle of Cyclic Quadrilateral

The exterior angle formed by extending one side of a cyclic quadrilateral is equal to the interior opposite angle.

Ptolemy's Theorem

For a cyclic quadrilateral with sides a, b, c, d and diagonals p, q, the product of the diagonals is equal to the sum of the products of opposite sides: p × q = (a × c) + (b × d).</p

questions.question: Working for 10 hours per day, 6 men can build a wall in a certain number of days. By working for how many hours per day can 12 men build the wall in the same days?

For a fixed amount of work, the number of workers is inversely proportional to the time taken (Days or Hours). If workers double, time taken is halved.

Total Work is often measured in Man-Hours or Man-Days. Total Work = Number of Men × Number of Days × Hours per day.</p

questions.question: Which of the following numbers is divisible by 11?

Divisibility by 3 and 9

A number is divisible by 3 (or 9) if the sum of all its digits is divisible by 3 (or 9).

Divisibility by 7

Subtract twice the last digit from the number formed by the remaining digits; the result should be divisible by 7.

Divisibility by 13

questions.question: It is given that ∆ABC ≅ ∆PQR, AB = 5 cm, ∠B = 40°, and ∠A = 80°. Which of the following options is true?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Congruent triangles ΔABC ≅ ΔPQR means corresponding sides and angles are equal.

Side AB corresponds to side PQ ⇒ PQ = AB = 5 cm.

In ΔABC, ∠C = 180° − (∠A + ∠B) = 180° − (80° + 40°) = 60°.

∠R corresponds to ∠C ⇒ ∠R = ∠C = 60°.

**∴ The correct answer is PQ = 5 cm and ∠R = 60°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** ΔABC ≅ ΔPQR, AB = 5 cm, ∠B = 40°, ∠A = 80°.

**Formula:** Angle sum property of a triangle (∠A + ∠B + ∠C = 180°) and CPCT (Corresponding Parts of Congruent Triangles).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/144298b4e113d1bcb9b049dc967fe493aa8eed644ea2eeaa07971489daf6cbde.png] 

⇒ In ΔABC, sum of angles = 180°

⇒ ∠A + ∠B + ∠C = 180°

⇒ 80° + 40° + ∠C = 180°

⇒ 120° + ∠C = 180°

⇒ ∠C = 60°

⇒ Since ΔABC ≅ ΔPQR, by CPCT:

⇒ PQ = AB = 5 cm

⇒ ∠P = ∠A = 80°, ∠Q = ∠B = 40°, ∠R = ∠C = 60°

**∴ The correct answer is PQ = 5 cm and ∠R = 60°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Congruence Rule (CPCT)

CPCT stands for Corresponding Parts of Congruent Triangles. If two triangles are congruent, then all their corresponding sides and angles are equal.

Angle Sum Property

The sum of all interior angles of any triangle is always 180°. If two angles are known, the third can be found as 180° − (Sum of known angles).

Criteria for Congruence

Two triangles can be proven congruent using SSS (Side-Side-Side), SAS (Side-Angle-Side), ASA (Angle-Side-Angle), AAS (Angle-Angle-Side), or RHS (Right angle-Hypotenuse-Side).</p

questions.question: How many kilogram of rice costing Rs. 60 per kg must be mixed with 24 kg of rice costing Rs. 42 per kg so that there may be a gain of 12% by selling the mixture at Rs. 56 per kg?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Find Cost Price (CP) of mixture: 56 ÷ 1.12 = ₹50/kg.

Apply Alligation ratio (Type 1 : Type 2) = (50 − 42) : (60 − 50) = 8 : 10 = 4 : 5.

Compare units: 5 units correspond to 24 kg.

Calculate Type 1: (24 ÷ 5) × 4 = 19.2 kg.

**∴ The correct answer is 19.2 kg.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

CP of first variety (Rice₁) = ₹60/kg

CP of second variety (Rice₂) = ₹42/kg

Quantity of second variety (Q₂) = 24 kg

Selling Price of mixture (SPₘᵢₓ) = ₹56/kg

Profit percentage = 12%

**Formula Used:**

CP = (SP × 100) ÷ (100 + Profit%)

Alligation Rule: (Quantity₁) ÷ (Quantity₂) = (Mean Price − CP₂) ÷ (CP₁ − Mean Price)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/24bb577a761ad60985eaf2f4bac0327ae9087bc7b4c6b4fd2167b7bacc1f3af8.png] 

⇒ Mean CP of Mixture = (56 × 100) ÷ (100 + 12)

⇒ Mean CP = 5600 ÷ 112 = ₹50/kg

⇒ Applying Alligation: Q₁ ÷ Q₂ = (50 − 42) ÷ (60 − 50)

⇒ Q₁ ÷ 24 = 8 ÷ 10

⇒ Q₁ ÷ 24 = 4 ÷ 5

⇒ Q₁ = (4 × 24) ÷ 5

⇒ Q₁ = 96 ÷ 5 = 19.2 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 19.2 kg.**

**__Additional Information__**

Alligation Method

Used to find the ratio in which two ingredients with different costs must be mixed to produce a mixture of a desired average cost.

Cost Price from Selling Price

Always calculate the CP of the mixture before using the Alligation rule if only the SP and profit/loss % are provided: CP = SP ÷ (1 ± r/100).

Weighted Average Formula

The mean price can also be verified using: Mean Price = (n₁c₁ + n₂c₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂), where n is quantity and c is cost.

questions.question: Rajnish borrowed ₹1,500 from a bank and repaid the entire amount with interest in two equal annual instalments, the first instalment being paid a year after Rajnish borrowed from the bank. If the rate of interest was 40% per annum, compounded annually, then what was the value (in ₹) of each instalment paid by Rajnish?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Rate of Interest = 40% = 2/5

Principal : Instalment ratio for Year 1 = 5 : 7

Principal : Instalment ratio for Year 2 = 5² : 7² = 25 : 49

To equate instalments, multiply Year 1 ratio by 7 → 35 : 49

Total Principal = 35 + 25 = 60 units ⇒ 60 units = ₹1500 ⇒ 1 unit = ₹25

Value of each instalment = 49 units = 49 × 25 = ₹1225

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1225.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Principal (P) = ₹1500

Rate (R) = 40% per annum

Time (n) = 2 years

**Formula Used:**

P = x / (1 + R/100)¹ + x / (1 + R/100)², where x is the value of each instalment.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13fd8384375d3900dbdb77c6e311a0169b6f28ec097bcff22a153f372562798.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 1500 = x / (1 + 40/100) + x / (1 + 40/100)²

⇒ 1500 = x / (1.4) + x / (1.96)

⇒ 1500 = x / (7/5) + x / (49/25)

⇒ 1500 = 5x / 7 + 25x / 49

⇒ 1500 = (35x + 25x) / 49

⇒ 1500 = 60x / 49

⇒ x = (1500 × 49) / 60

⇒ x = 25 × 49

⇒ x = 1225

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1225.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Compound Interest Instalment Formula

For 'n' years with annual instalment 'x', Principal P = x × [1/(1+r) + 1/(1+r)² + ... + 1/(1+r)ⁿ], where r = R/100.

Effective Interest Rate

For 2 years compounded annually, the effective rate Rₑff = R₁ + R₂ + (R₁ × R₂)/100.

Simple Interest Instalment

In SI, the instalment x = (100 × Amount) / [100t + rt(t−1)/2], where t is the number of years.

questions.question: A sum triple itself in 9 years at simple interest. Find the rate of interest per annum is.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Rate (R) = [(n − 1) × 100] ÷ T

Where n = number of times the sum becomes (n = 3) and T = Time (T = 9 years).

R = [(3 − 1) × 100] ÷ 9

R = 200 ÷ 9 = 22²/₉%

**∴ The correct answer is 22²/₉%.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Let Principal (P) = P

Amount (A) = 3P (Since the sum triples itself)

Time (T) = 9 years

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

Amount (A) = Principal (P) + Simple Interest (SI)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/76acbb5040afb9734a91b27423d0afd9ccf9578245a14be2b58040dc667fe40f.png] 

⇒ SI = Amount − Principal

⇒ SI = 3P − P = 2P

⇒ 2P = (P × R × 9) ÷ 100

⇒ 2 = (R × 9) ÷ 100

⇒ 200 = 9R

⇒ R = 200 ÷ 9

⇒ R = 22²/₉%

**∴ The correct answer is 22²/₉%.**

**__Additional Information__**

Simple Interest Principle

In simple interest, the interest remains constant every year because it is always calculated on the original Principal (P).

Relationship between Time and Multiplier

If a sum becomes 'n' times in T years, then T = [(n − 1) × 100] ÷ R. This allows for quick calculation of either Rate or Time.

Simple Interest vs Compound Interest

For the first year, SI and CI are equal if the interest is compounded annually. From the second year onwards, CI > SI because interest is earned on interest in CI.</p

questions.question: (sin θ + cosec θ)² + (cos θ + sec θ)² = ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Put θ = 45° to find the value of the expression quickly.

Expression = (sin 45° + cosec 45°)² + (cos 45° + sec 45°)²

⇒ (1/√2 + √2)² + (1/√2 + √2)² = (3/√2)² + (3/√2)² = 9/2 + 9/2 = 9

Checking Option 3: 7 + tan²45° + cot²45° = 7 + (1)² + (1)² = 9

**∴ The correct answer is 7 + tan²θ + cot²θ.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** (sin θ + cosec θ)² + (cos θ + sec θ)²

**Formula Used:** (a + b)² = a² + b² + 2ab; sin²θ + cos²θ = 1; 1 + tan²θ = sec²θ; 1 + cot²θ = cosec²θ

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f4c99d02a47fb7cbdf27c569996d65320131564390dfd75b55dafaf93de5ca73.png] 

Expanding the given expression:

⇒ (sin²θ + cosec²θ + 2 sin θ cosec θ) + (cos²θ + sec²θ + 2 cos θ sec θ)

Since sin θ × cosec θ = 1 and cos θ × sec θ = 1:

⇒ sin²θ + cosec²θ + 2(1) + cos²θ + sec²θ + 2(1)

Grouping the terms:

⇒ (sin²θ + cos²θ) + cosec²θ + sec²θ + 4

⇒ 1 + (1 + cot²θ) + (1 + tan²θ) + 4

⇒ 1 + 1 + cot²θ + 1 + tan²θ + 4

⇒ 7 + tan²θ + cot²θ

**∴ The correct answer is 7 + tan²θ + cot²θ.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Fundamental Trigonometric Identities

There are three main identities: sin²θ + cos²θ = 1, 1 + tan²θ = sec²θ, and 1 + cot²θ = cosec²θ.

Reciprocal Relations

cosec θ = 1/sin θ, sec θ = 1/cos θ, and cot θ = 1/tan θ. Their products (e.g., sin θ × cosec θ) are always equal to 1.

Algebraic Expansion

For any trigonometric terms, (x + y)² = x² + y² + 2xy. This is frequently used to simplify squared sums of ratios.</p
